title: Exam Week
subtitle: Ten weeks of English, one paper.
objectives: Recall the three tenses from weeks 1 to 5
Recall word parts and phrasal verbs
Recall the Don Quixote chapters 11 to 20
Sit a full-length paper at exam pace

cards.title: Ten weeks of English, one paper
cards.text: Twenty-four questions. Longer than a normal week, because the real one will be.

cards.title: Tenses, and sentences that finish
cards.text: Past, future, and the rule that holds them together.
points: **Regular past adds -ed.** Irregular verbs change shape.
**Will** for a decision now, **going to** for an existing plan.
**Phrasal verbs:** the particle carries the meaning.
**A sentence needs** a subject, a verb and a finished thought.

options: Yesterday he will catch the bus.
question.explain: Catch is irregular: caught. And 'yesterday' forces the past.

cards.title: Word parts, comparison and phrases
cards.text: How to read a new word, and how to add detail precisely.
points: **Prefix changes meaning; suffix changes the job.**
**Short words take -er/-est; long words take more/most.**
**Never both:** 'more faster' is wrong.
**A descriptive phrase** goes next to the noun it describes.

cards.title: One more pass before the paper
cards.text: Eight irregular verbs. Tap each one and say the past form before you read it.

options: He is more strong than me.
He is strongest of the two.

cards.title: Good spot to pause
cards.text: Two blocks reviewed, one to go, then the paper.

cards.title: Adverbs, and choosing the form
cards.text: What a word points at decides which form it takes.
points: **Adverbs answer** how, when, where, how often.
**Describing a thing** → adjective. **Describing an action** → adverb.
**good/well** is the pair that catches people.
**'Only' moves** and the meaning moves with it.

cards.title: One repair, most of the grammar
cards.text: If a rule slips, write out a fan repair and the forms sort themselves.
points: **I unplugged it.** Regular past.
**I took the guard off.** Irregular past, phrasal verb, split.
**The bearing was noisy; it ran noisily.** Adjective, then adverb.
**I am going to oil it.** An existing plan.

cards.title: Chapters 11 to 20, in one line each
cards.text: If a question names a chapter, this is the thread.
points: **11–13:** the barber's basin, the freed prisoners, the mountains.
**14–15:** the letter to Dulcinea, lost, then invented.
**16–17:** home on an ox-cart, fussed over by friends.
**18–20:** the search, the players, the Knight of the Mirrors.

cards.title: The night before still matters
cards.text: None of this is about being clever on the day.
points: **Sleep beats cramming.**
**Eat something.** Your brain runs on glucose.
**Read the whole question** before touching an option.
**Mark the hard one and move on.**

cards.title: The four threads
points: Tenses: finished, planned, or habitual.
Word parts: prefix for meaning, suffix for job.
Comparison and phrases: precision, placed correctly.
Adjective or adverb: ask what it points at.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 11 English, the practice paper. Twenty-four questions across all ten teaching weeks, grouped in the review by thread rather than week: tenses, word parts, precision, and the adjective-or-adverb decision. The irregular verb interactive returns so the last thing he does before the paper is recall forms actively rather than read a list. One lens card compresses Don Quixote chapters 11 to 20 into a line each, since literature questions are the ones most easily lost to simple forgetting of plot.
discussion: Which four threads does the term reduce to?
Which tense rule still catches you?
Can you summarise each chapter in a line?
extension: Sit the quiz once at pace, then again days later without revising.
Write one exam question per thread.
misconceptions: That revision means re-reading rather than self-testing.
That the literature questions need no preparation.
